decisions: Package name: boltforge. GitHub account: alihossainhabib. Repository links use alihossainhabib/boltforge without assuming the repo exists — the user will create it.
No go_router/auto_route dependency — Navigator 1.0 onGenerateRoute used to minimize the generated project's dependency surface.
Feature-generated files live at lib/features/<feature>/... — the same location as the auth flow.
Removed the `recase` dependency from pubspec.yaml — confirmed zero usages anywhere in the codebase; would have only cost pub.dev score points for no benefit.

Dart SDK constraint in pubspec.yaml is the user's own confirmed value ('>=3.0.0 <4.0.0'), validated against a real Dart 3.2.6 install — left untouched since there is no technical reason found to raise it.
DI auto-registration uses stable marker comments inserted via string replacement, not a Dart AST parser.
A missing service_locator.dart or missing marker comments is a warning, not a hard failure of `generate`; a duplicate registration is a hard error (exit code 1).

CI runs on both ubuntu-latest and windows-latest specifically because this project has real history of a bug that only manifested on Windows — a single-OS CI matrix was judged insufficient given that history.

example/ contains a terminal walkthrough (README.md) rather than an importable .dart file, since boltforge is a CLI tool with no meaningful library API to demonstrate — the walkthrough mirrors the user's own confirmed-working command sequence rather than an invented one.
release.yml was deliberately not created this round — not requested, and better designed once an actual release/publish process exists to model rather than guessed at now.

Package resource resolution (templatesRoot) uses Isolate.resolvePackageUri rather than Platform.script — found via a real end-to-end CLI run outside the test suite, now also confirmed fixed by a second real end-to-end run.
